HEEWON STYLE — a premium KOREAN WEBTOON / MANHWA splash illustration of a group, lit with cinematic tenebrism. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). WAIST-UP GROUP SHOT of three, faces large, staggered in depth. DRAW IT EXACTLY IN THE STYLE OF THE ATTACHED CHARACTER SHEET: the same clean confident black ink linework, the same manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair). It must read as an INKED DRAWING: visible line strokes everywhere — bold tapered contour lines around every figure, drawn fold lines in the silk and armour, hair drawn as inked strands, a little cross-hatching and line shading in the shadows — then flat cel-shading in two or three tones per colour, no airbrushed gradients. Each face must be recognisably the character drawn on the sheet, wearing the same clothes. NOT realistic, NOT an oil painting, NOT photoreal, NOT painterly, NOT a 3D render, no skin pores or photographic texture. ONLY THESE THREE PEOPLE in the frame. THE THREE WOMEN AT THE ROOT OF THREE KINGDOMS, shoulder to shoulder, each lit from her own side. Alyoung of Silla on the left, calm and wise, a pale dawn light; Sosuno in the centre, fierce, arms folded, a dusty-gold key (#e8a04a); Queen Heo of Gaya on the right, serene and foreign, red sail-cloth over one shoulder, a red key. CHARACTER SHEET (copy these faces, hair and clothes exactly): LEFT of the sheet = LADY ALYOUNG; MIDDLE of the sheet = SOSUNO; RIGHT of the sheet = QUEEN HU. LADY ALYOUNG — Crown: Silla gold crown, copied from the attached Cheonmachong museum photo: a broad sheet-gold band with three tall tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 (three tiers of short arms turned up into heart-shaped tips) and two antler uprights at the sides, hung with hundreds of round gold spangles on wires and many curved pale-green jade gogok, two long chains of gold leaf pendants falling from the temples to the collarbones. Thin bright sheet gold, never a European spiked crown, never a solid cast crown or a tiara. Colour #a8c8f0. | SOSUNO — Look: Long straight black hair with a high topknot pinned by her gold binyeo, a thin red headband with a center jewel; sharp brows, cool appraising eyes. Dress: Dusty-rose hanbok over white sleeves, black wrap sash with red cords, red-wrapped wrists; bow and quiver on her back. Her hex is lamplight or a ground stamp — never gold robes. Colour #e8a04a. | QUEEN HU — Look: South Indian princess from Ayuta: deep warm brown skin, clearly darker than every Gaya and Samhan face around her; large dark kohl-lined eyes, full lips, straight nose, blue-black hair coiled low with the purple-tiger binyeo, small gold hoop earrings. Dress: Her portrait silk: violet-purple jeogori with magenta-gold patterned sleeves and cream cuffs, deep violet chima, pale gold sash with tassels. Cut close and tailored: the jacket fitted to the bust and waist, the sash cinched high, the skirt falling clean from the hips; elegant and expensive, never loose, never a sari dump, never pink. Colour #d98fa8. LIGHT AND BACKGROUND (deep manhwa tenebrism, darker than a normal splash page): about TWO-THIRDS OF THE FRAME IS PURE INK-BLACK. No set, no architecture or floor beyond what the scene names, no props beyond what the characters hold. Each figure is pulled out of the black by ONE hard, narrow key light from the side or from below in THAT PERSON'S OWN COLOUR, catching only a cheekbone, an eye, the bridge of the nose, the edge of a sleeve, a plate of armour or a hand; the rest of each figure falls off into solid black shadow and merges with the background, so neighbouring figures are separated only by their coloured edge light. MOSTLY IN DARKNESS: each figure is about TWO-THIRDS BLACK SILHOUETTE; only the side of the face, shoulder, hands and robe edge turned toward that person's own light show colour and detail, the rest merges into the black. SPLIT LIGHTING ON EVERY FIGURE: the lit side of each face and body in that person's colour, the other half PURE BLACK; no even front light, no fill light, no evenly lit robes — even white silk falls to black on its shadow side. Faces readable but half in shadow, eyes catching the light (ordinary eyes — no light streaks or glow across the eyes). At most a few thin wisps of smoke tinted by those coloured lights. Deep inky blacks, crisp highlights, hard cast shadows. Each person's colour is the colour of the light on them — never a glow aura, halo or outline glow. BLOCKING, BODY LANGUAGE AND FACIAL EXPRESSIONS show who they are to each other at a glance. Faces and clothes from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. One of each person, never cloned. No text, no lettering, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
